title: CLO 2025.0 - Virtual Model IK Joint Mapping
description: In version 2025.0, the IK joint mapping feature for virtual models allows you to more easily implement your designs using various virtual models in CLO.

summary: ```markdown # CLO 2025.0 - Virtual Model IK Joint Mapping ## Introduction This video introduces the virtual model IK joint printing function. In this version, we have introduced the virtual model IK joint printing function, which allows the virtual model to be imported from outside to utilize the actions and postures provided by CLO. Let’s take a look at the IK joint printing function together. ## Supported File Types IK joint printing is currently only supported for FBX files with Google information. ## Important Considerations Before Printing Before importing, it is essential to note some important points regarding IK printing: - FBX files should not have repeated name joints. - Virtual models must include joints such as shoulders, elbows, wrists, pelvis, knees, and ankles. - The T-position is the standard position for reference for IK printing. IK printing with incorrect positioning may lead to errors. Therefore, it is necessary to correctly set the virtual model to the T-position. ### Adjusting to T-Position If the virtual model is not in T-position, you need to manually adjust the joint points of the virtual model in the 3D window to achieve T-position. 1. In the virtual model information display in the 3D vertical menu bar, open the virtual model joint point. 2. Press the joint point of the virtual model and adjust it to T-position. **Note:** For non-humanoid images or four-legged animal virtual models, IK printing may not be correctly applied. ## Printing the IK Joint To print the IK joint to the virtual model: 1. In the main menu bar, find the virtual model editor under the virtual model section. 2. Select the IK joint option card. ### Setting T-Position Once your virtual model is in T-position, press the "Set T-position" button in the upper right corner to identify the adjusted T-position. If the setting is completed correctly, the reset position button on the right will be activated. This button can help you restore the original position after adjusting during the IK printing process. ## Methods of Printing Joints There are two main ways to print the joint: 1. **Manual Printing**: You can manually print each joint. 2. **Automatic Printing**: You can automatically print the joint by identifying the name of the joint. ### Manual Joint Printing To manually print the joint: 1. Start by examining the joint list, which is divided into required and selected categories. 2. The corresponding joint names are listed under these categories. To ensure accuracy, you must print the desired type of IK joint. - For example, you must print all required parts. The selected parts are optional but will provide more accurate movements if the virtual model includes these joints. #### Printing Process - Click on the name of the joint to preview its location in the virtual model. - You can also click on the joint in the preview to find its corresponding position. - Select the appropriate joint in the 3D window, or first click on the joint in the virtual model and then in the option card to print it. **Note:** If multiple joints overlap, you can choose which joint to print. After printing, the printing area will be displayed in green in the 3D window and the virtual model editor. ## Managing Joint Printing - In the joint list, a white contrast mark on the left side of the joint indicates that the joint printing is complete. - The name of the joint saved for the virtual model will be displayed next to the printing box on the right. ### Re-selecting Joints If you misprint a joint and want to re-select it, you can do so by: - Selecting the joint in the joint list or the preview, then clicking on another joint to re-print it. - Alternatively, select the joint in the joint list or the preview, press the Delete key on your keyboard, and then re-select the correct joint point. ## Symmetrical Joint Printing When printing the left joint, the right one will also be printed if symmetrical printing is not utilized in the upper right corner of the virtual model editor. To enable symmetrical printing: - The joint names must be designated as left and right, or use letters L and R or lowercase l and r, separated by an underscore. - You can select the joint point and modify the name in the virtual editor. If symmetrical printing is not enabled, you will need to manually print the left and right joints separately. ## Completing Joint Printing Once all required joints are printed, the state on the right side of the project will be displayed as complete, indicating that the IK printing is finished. ## Automatic Joint Printing To automatically print the joints: 1. Press the reset button at the top to reset all currently printed joints. 2. Press the auto-print button at the bottom to automatically print all required joints. **Note:** The auto-printing function will only work correctly when the joint names of the virtual model match those in the virtual model file or when the virtual model file is from DeathMiximoCharacterCreator or MetaHuman. ## Saving IK Joint Printing Information The information of the IK joint printing of the virtual model can be stored as an IKS file. You can click on "Save" and "Open" in the upper right corner to save the IK data as an IKS file or to open a stored IKS file. After completing all joint printing, you can directly apply the available posture. **Important Note:** IKS files only have the same structure and are integrated between virtual models of the same printing method. You will see that the posture has been correctly applied, and the virtual model file of the IK joint printing can be stored in a format that can be reused. By utilizing the new IK joint printing function in the virtual model editor, you can more easily use various virtual models in the cloud to realize your design. ```
